title: Find Confidence, Avoid Ego
coreMove: Earned confidence keeps ego away from your position: check competence, values, feedback, and discomfort, then revise without making every correction a trial of your worth.

exampleSpecs.audience: shift leads who treat corrections as personal attacks
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wrong till count can either start defensiveness or improve the next shift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show the same person before and after separating ego from position

exampleSpecs.audience: operations leads who confuse showy action with courage
exampleSpecs.stakes: bulk orders look bold but may waste cash and storage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one reviewed record shifts the meaning of boldness

exampleSpecs.audience: technicians who spiral after a visible mistake
exampleSpecs.stakes: a returned repair can become blame, shame, or a clean correction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: let the protagonist's own thoughts move from defense to clean repair

exampleSpecs.audience: public service managers allocating scarce attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: time can be spent on praise-seeking or on error review
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: keep the whole scene in the pre-action allocation of time

exampleSpecs.audience: supply leads balancing speed with accuracy
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bad count can slow preparation now or create a risk for the next shift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: make the two-bad-options tension explicit and resolve through correction

exampleSpecs.audience: performers who confuse volume with courage
exampleSpecs.stakes: a solo can sound brave while still being unready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: let the lesson arise through two people talking
